svg.title: Zane Wang — building tools that make AI coding agents more reliable
svg.desc: A pixel-art sunset over a city drawn from the past 12 months of Zane's GitHub contributions. As the image loads, the contribution graph appears along the horizon and rises into the city: one building per week, taller when the week was busier, and one window per day, lit on the 299 days he contributed. A gold pennant flies over each week in which one of his pull requests was merged upstream (7 weeks, 12 PRs). Below the city, the tools he maintains: claudemem, memory that lasts across agent sessions (about 11,000 lines of Go and nearly as many in tests); handoff, which lets a strong model delegate to cheaper ones through resumable specs, with a published evaluation; dev-orchestrator, a Claude Code plugin that takes a task to a tested pull request, failing test first. Then 12 PRs merged into 10 upstream projects (Apr – Aug 2026), 10 bug fixes and 2 small features: axum, SQLx and goose in Rust; AnyIO, Tenacity and Feast in Python; Zod, TanStack Query, Fastify and Claude HUD in JavaScript and TypeScript. He uses AI to find and draft fixes, verifies each one locally, and sees it through maintainer review. His production background covers multimodal evaluation and high-volume data systems; his current public focus is tools for reliable AI coding agents.
